description: Library of colour RELATIONSHIPS (not palettes): how two or more colours, lights or surfaces relate. Labels EVIDENCE / CRAFT / DERIVED / HYPOTHESIS. Source keys are in sources_color.json (new) or SOURCE_REGISTRY.json / ai-visual-artist research (existing). Nothing has been generated yet (test_status untested).

entries.name: Warm light / cool shadow
entries.label: EVIDENCE+CRAFT
entries.purpose: Outdoor sun: the lit side takes the warm sun colour, shadows are filled by blue skylight; reads as daylight and gives depth.
entries.how: Key from sun side, lit planes h~60-80 (OKLCH) slightly warm; shadow planes shift toward h~230-260 and lose ~30-50% chroma; keep the shift on every object incl. skin so it reads as light. Prompt: 'warm late sun from left, cool sky-blue shadows'.
entries.limits: Overcast or indoor single-source scenes have no blue skylight fill; overdoing the blue looks like a filter. Craft magnitudes are not measured.

entries.name: Cool window key / warm bounce
entries.label: CRAFT+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Indoor north-window light with a wooden floor/table bouncing warm light into shadows; calm, natural shop/home feel.
entries.how: Key = window (neutral-cool), fill = warm bounce from below (wood, sand, kraft paper); underside of chin/frame and shadow side gain h~60-80 at low chroma.
entries.limits: Bounce strength depends on surface area and distance; in AI images the bounce is often missing and must be asked for.

entries.name: Warm practical pool in cool darkness
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: Night interior: a lamp/sign makes a small warm pool; the rest of the frame is cool and dark. Isolation, intimacy, mystery.
entries.how: Low key (notan mostly dark); one practical source h~70-85, moderate C; ambient h~240-260, C<=0.04; soft falloff at the pool edge; characters step in/out of the pool on story beats.
entries.limits: Too many practicals destroy the pool; the warm area must stay small relative to the frame.

entries.name: Golden hour: low warm sun, long blue shadows
entries.label: EVIDENCE+CRAFT
entries.purpose: Low sun passes through more atmosphere (warmer); shadows lit by the remaining blue sky look strongly blue; romantic, nostalgic.
entries.how: Raking light 5-15 deg; warm side h~55-70 high chroma; shadow h~240 visibly blue; long cast shadows as composition lines (Hua Hin beach promo).
entries.limits: Mood link is associative/cultural; the warm side can turn skin orange - protect skin hue.

entries.name: Mixed daylight + tungsten in one frame
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Two sources of different CCT: camera or viewer can neutralise only one; the other side keeps a cast. Use for cosy contrast, avoid for product truth.
entries.how: Mood: let the window side go blue and the lamp side orange on purpose. Product colour: switch off one source or gel them to match; set WB on a neutral card under the key.
entries.limits: Auto-WB averages the two and gets neither right; product colour then shifts across the frame.

entries.name: Shadows lean toward the complement of the light
entries.label: CRAFT+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Under a strongly coloured key, neutral shadow areas look tinted toward the opposite hue (contrast/adaptation); painters exaggerate it to make light feel coloured.
entries.how: Warm key: push shadow hue 150-180 deg away at low chroma (C 0.02-0.05); magenta neon key: shadows slightly green-teal.
entries.limits: Exaggeration is a style choice; physically shadows are lit by whatever ambient light exists, which may not be the complement.

entries.name: Blue hour: cool ambient, warm windows
entries.label: EVIDENCE+CRAFT
entries.purpose: After sunset the sky light is deep blue; windows and signs read warm and inviting by contrast.
entries.how: Ambient h~250-265, mid-low key; windows and shop sign h~70-85; make the lit shop facade the warmest, brightest area for a 'come in' feel.
entries.limits: Short window in real shoots; in AI images keep sky and window light consistent.

entries.name: Colour bleed from ground to underside
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Light reflected from a coloured surface tints nearby surfaces facing it (mutual illumination); grounds objects in the scene.
entries.how: Cutout frame on a coloured table/cloth: add a soft gradient of the ground colour on the lower rim and temple insides (HTML layer, multiply/soft-light, opacity 10-25%), strongest where closest.
entries.limits: Weak on dark or matte-black surfaces; overdone it looks like a coloured glow.

entries.name: Inside corners deepen colour
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: In a concave fold (inside of a case, a book gutter) light bounces back and forth so colour deepens; vision expects this.
entries.how: Case shots: inside corners of a coloured lining darker and more saturated than the flat floor; paper props: gutters slightly richer.
entries.limits: Depends on perceived shape; flat-shaded AI renders often miss it.

entries.name: Metal frames show the environment, not a local colour
entries.label: EVIDENCE+CRAFT
entries.purpose: Polished metal has almost no diffuse local colour; you see the environment reflected and tinted by the metal (gold, rose, gunmetal).
entries.how: Plan reflections: a light card for a bright rim, a dark flag for a defining dark line; gold = reflections tinted warm; a coloured card puts an accent into the rim.
entries.limits: On flat backgrounds metal looks dull grey; cutouts carry reflections from the original shoot that may contradict the new scene.

entries.name: Specular highlights carry the light colour
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: On dielectrics (acetate, TR90, lens surface) the highlight has the colour of the light, not the object; viewers use highlights as an illumination cue.
entries.how: Red acetate under warm key: highlight warm-white, never pink; keep highlight hue identical across all objects in the frame.
entries.limits: Metals tint their highlights; coated lenses add coating colour to reflections.

entries.name: Lenses and mirror coatings take the scene's colours
entries.label: CRAFT+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Lenses reflect the environment; mirror coatings reflect strongly. An empty-looking lens breaks realism (house rule: cutouts get a lens layer).
entries.how: Lens layer with a faint, blurred, perspective-warped reflection of the brightest scene area (window/sky), opacity 10-30%, plus a thin specular arc; mirror lenses show a distorted scene in the coating tint.
entries.limits: AR residual reflection colour differs by product; copy the real lens, do not invent a hue.

entries.name: Local colour lives in the lit half-tone
entries.label: EVIDENCE+CRAFT
entries.purpose: Observers estimate an object's lightness from its brightest parts excluding highlights; that plane shows the true local colour best.
entries.how: Turn the frame so the rim front takes direct but non-specular light; leave that plane untouched when correcting; judge 'is the colour right' only there.
entries.limits: Strong coloured ambient (sunset) shifts even that plane - then add a neutral reference shot.

entries.name: Distance shifts toward the air colour
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Scattering between viewer and far objects lowers contrast and pulls colour toward the sky/haze colour: a depth cue.
entries.how: Per depth plane: raise L, lower C, shift h toward the sky colour; foreground keeps the darkest darks and highest chroma.
entries.limits: Clear dry air or night scenes show little shift; misuse makes everything foggy.

entries.name: Grey/clear product shifts toward the background's complement
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: A neutral product (smoke-grey TR90, clear acetate, silver) on a saturated ground looks tinted toward the complementary hue and shifted in lightness opposite to the ground.
entries.how: If true colour matters include a shot on a neutral ground (L~0.85-0.92, C~0); otherwise pick a ground whose induced shift flatters the frame (cool ground warms a brown frame).
entries.limits: Grows with ground area and chroma; outlines alter it.

entries.name: Same tone looks lighter on dark, darker on light
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Lightness is judged relative to surroundings; a black frame on black velvet loses its edge, a grey frame on black looks lighter.
entries.how: Dark frames on mid-light grounds; light/clear frames on mid-dark grounds; check in notan view.
entries.limits: Edge highlights can rescue dark-on-dark; low-key mood shots may want the merge on purpose.

entries.name: Fine lines spread their colour (assimilation)
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Thin dense pattern lines pull the colour of the area they cross toward themselves instead of contrasting with it.
entries.how: Charcoal carousels: tint under dense dark hatching reads duller/darker; light hatching lightens an area without changing its fill; brand green under black texture reads near-black.
entries.limits: At wide line spacing it turns into contrast; viewing size decides which effect wins.

entries.name: Equal-luminance complements vibrate
entries.label: CRAFT+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Two saturated hues at nearly equal luminance (red on green, blue on orange) give an unstable edge and poor legibility because the luminance channel carries no edge.
entries.how: Avoid for text and product edges; keep it small if wanted (poster, discord moment); else separate the pair by >=0.25 OKLCH L or add a neutral outline.
entries.limits: The 'vibration' claim is craft; the legibility loss follows from WCAG luminance contrast.

entries.name: A busy colourful surround mutes the centre
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: A surround with high chromatic variance lowers perceived contrast of the region inside it compared with a uniform surround of the same average.
entries.how: A product on a busy colourful scene looks less vivid than on a calm one; simplify or blur the surround (house rule: calm backgrounds).
entries.limits: Measured on lab patterns; magnitude in photos unknown.

entries.name: Bright/warm scene after a long dark/cool one feels stronger
entries.label: EVIDENCE+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Adaptation and afterimages from the previous shot shift the next one toward the opposite; relief needs less grading.
entries.how: Place the relief beat after a cool low-key stretch of several seconds; grade it only moderately warm; preview cuts in sequence, never only as stills. Carousels: dark slide then bright slide.
entries.limits: Very short shots give little effect; exact durations not verified.

entries.name: Whites drift after adaptation
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: After minutes in warm light, warm whites look white; after a long warm sequence a neutral shot looks bluish. Full adaptation takes minutes.
entries.how: Before a product reveal in a long warm sequence, re-introduce a neutral or cool shot; in grading sessions rest on a neutral grey screen.
entries.limits: Viewer room light and night-shift settings are uncontrolled.

entries.name: Saturated reds/blues look brighter than they measure
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Helmholtz-Kohlrausch: at equal luminance, saturated colours (esp. blue, red) look brighter than greys/yellows, so the eye overrates their contrast.
entries.how: Always measure text contrast with color_tools.py contrast; do not trust the eye for red/blue price tags; a saturated blue accent feels heavier than its L.
entries.limits: Magnitude varies by observer and condition; mechanism debated.

entries.name: Familiar objects are judged against memory colours
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Skin, sky, foliage, fruit are seen biased toward their typical colour and act as references viewers use to decide whether an image is off.
entries.how: Grade freely but keep skin in a believable range (vectorscope skin line); a familiar object (hand, leaf, white paper) near the product is a silent reference.
entries.limits: Strongest on the blue-yellow axis; memory colours differ between people and cultures.

entries.name: Ambiguous illumination splits viewers (#TheDress)
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: When pixel colours lie on the daylight (blue-yellow) axis and illumination cues are missing, viewers silently assume different lights and see different object colours.
entries.how: Navy, tortoise, brown/blue tinted lenses on plain grounds are high risk: add directional shadow, skin in the same light, a white reference; check at thumbnail size.
entries.limits: Colours off the daylight axis (green/purple) are far less ambiguous.

entries.name: A tint on everything reads as light; on one object reads as colour
entries.label: EVIDENCE+DERIVED
entries.purpose: A cast applied to the whole scene including skin is attributed to the illuminant; a cast only on the object changes the object's colour.
entries.how: Time of day / mood: grade globally (bg, props, skin, product). 'This product is special': tint or glow only the product. Do not tint only the background if the product should look correctly lit.
entries.limits: Strong global casts still shift product colour for some viewers; keep one neutral shot.

entries.name: Big areas look different from small swatches
entries.label: EVIDENCE+CRAFT
entries.purpose: Appearance and interpretation change with area/image size; large fields tend to read more intense than the chip they were picked from.
entries.how: Pick large background colours slightly calmer than the swatch you like; review every image at IG thumbnail size and full screen.
entries.limits: Size-effect magnitudes not quantified here.

entries.name: Chroma edges mark objects; luminance carries shading
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: In natural scenes chromatic and luminance contrast are statistically independent; chroma changes tend to mark object boundaries while luminance also changes with shadow.
entries.how: Separate the frame from the background by hue/chroma even when values are close (shading can stay natural); value for form/depth, chroma for 'a different thing'.
entries.limits: Not enough alone for legibility or CVD viewers; pair with value contrast for text and key edges.

entries.name: Green-magenta errors look worse than warm-cool errors
entries.label: DERIVED
entries.purpose: Observers are most uncertain along the blue-yellow (daylight) axis, so warm/cool shifts read as 'light' while green/magenta shifts read as 'wrong'.
entries.how: Correcting AI/phone images: fix tint (green-magenta) precisely first, then choose temperature for mood.
entries.limits: Derived from uncertainty data, not a direct test of grading tolerance.

entries.name: Warm/cool is relative to neighbours
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: A red-violet looks warm next to blue and cool next to orange; temperature contrast exists only in relation.
entries.how: Decide temperature by pairs that touch in the frame; when analyze_image warm_pct/cool_pct (fixed hue bins) disagrees with the feel, trust the pairwise judgement and note it.
entries.limits: Craft vocabulary; the warm-cool association itself is a robust colour-emotion dimension.

entries.name: Dominant / subordinate / accent
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: One hue family dominates by area, one supports, one small accent carries attention: unity with a focal point.
entries.how: Measure with analyze_image proportion_top3_pct; accent = smallest area, highest chroma, at the saliency peak; options 90/10, 70/20/10, 60/30/10.
entries.limits: 60-30-10 has no known origin; k-means counts area, not attention.

entries.name: Neutral field + one accent
entries.label: CRAFT+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Premium/editorial product look: near-neutral surroundings (C<0.02) with a single saturated element (coloured acetate frame or brand peach).
entries.how: Measured on our _example post: warm greys 93.6%, brand green 3.3%, black 2.5%, mean_chroma 0.009. For a colourful frame, let the frame be the only chromatic object.
entries.limits: Can feel cold for warm story content; neutrals still need value structure.

entries.name: Highest chroma reserved for the focal point
entries.label: CRAFT+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Saturation hierarchy: chroma steps down from subject to midground to background, guiding attention.
entries.how: Background C<=0.04, midground 0.04-0.08, subject highest; check that the strongest saliency peak sits on the subject.
entries.limits: Saliency models are not eye-tracking; a bright high-contrast low-chroma area can still win.

entries.name: Lightness contrast drives pair preference and legibility
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Pair preference depends strongly on how liked the component colours are and on lightness contrast; WCAG legibility also rests on luminance contrast.
entries.how: Any two colours that must be read together (text/bg, frame/bg) need a clear L difference (color_tools contrast); choose hue for meaning after L is set.
entries.limits: Patch studies, Western samples; whole-image effects weaker.

entries.name: Similar hues feel harmonious
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Harmony ratings rise with hue similarity; analogous and monochromatic are the best-supported 'harmony' schemes.
entries.how: Calm story slides and quote images: one hue family (+-30 deg OKLCH), interest from value and texture.
entries.limits: Harmonious is not the same as preferred or attention-getting; needs a value accent.

entries.name: Check multi-colour schemes pair by pair
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Three-colour harmony is approximately the average harmony of its three pairs; the shape on the wheel is not what matters.
entries.how: For triadic/tetradic palettes evaluate the pairs that actually touch in the layout; mute or separate the worst pair with a neutral.
entries.limits: Model built on colour wheels and interior images; extension beyond three colours suggested, not shown.

entries.name: Hue templates are idea generators, not quality rules
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Large theme datasets show little natural use of templates and no higher ratings for template-matching themes; 2-3 hues per 5-colour theme rated best.
entries.how: Generate candidates with color_tools harmony, then choose by value structure, context and testing in the composite.
entries.limits: Ratings were of context-free 5-colour themes.

entries.name: Complements with unequal area and chroma
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: Complementary pairs work when one dominates and the other is small or muted; equal amounts compete.
entries.how: Teal sea 70% muted + small saturated orange tortoise frame; or muted orange room + a small cool lens reflection.
entries.limits: Opposites on CIELAB/OKLCH wheels only approximate perceived complements.

entries.name: Analogous palettes need a wide value range
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: Neighbouring hues at similar lightness turn muddy and flat; a wide value range keeps form and focus.
entries.how: Spread L from ~0.25 to ~0.95 across the family; put the extreme L at the focal point.
entries.limits: High-key pastel styles compress value on purpose; then use edges/line for structure.

entries.name: Limited palette via mother colour or gamut mask
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: Restricting the gamut makes all parts feel lit by the same light and belong together.
entries.how: Mix a little of one 'mother' hue into every colour (HTML: overlay of that hue at 5-10%), or draw a gamut polygon on the OKLCH wheel and pick only inside it.
entries.limits: Overdone it becomes a monotone filter; brand colours may fall outside the mask.

entries.name: Discord: reversed natural value order
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: A hue made lighter than its natural order next to a naturally lighter hue (light violet beside darker yellow) creates tension; small doses enliven, large doses disturb.
entries.how: Check OKLCH L (natural order yellow > orange > red > blue/violet at max chroma); invert one pair in a small area for unease (night-optic ghost moment).
entries.limits: No scientific evidence for the emotional claim.

entries.name: Hues have a natural lightness order
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: At maximum sRGB chroma yellow is very light (L~0.97) and blue/violet dark (L~0.45); dark yellows become browns/mustards.
entries.how: Plan hues by available lightness: a dark accent cannot be vivid yellow, a light accent cannot be vivid blue; use OKLCH gamut-aware ramps.
entries.limits: sRGB-specific; wider gamuts move the limits.

entries.name: Colour liking follows what the colour is attached to
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: People like colours to the extent they like the objects associated with them; the same brown is pleasant as wood/coffee and unpleasant as rot.
entries.how: Judge a colour in its object context (brown acetate next to wood and leather); pick backgrounds whose associations support the product.
entries.limits: Associations vary by culture and person.

entries.name: Meaning is inferred relative to the other colours in the set
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: In legends/codes viewers assign colours to concepts by comparing all options, not only by the strongest association.
entries.how: Infographics (lens types, coatings): choose colours so each concept's best match is distinct within the set; test with the team without the legend.
entries.limits: Studied in visualisations; generalisation to ads untested.

entries.name: State colour emotion as association, not effect
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Colour-emotion associations are robust across cultures (for colour words) but causal effects on behaviour (red/performance, red/attractiveness) are small or vanish after bias correction.
entries.how: Write 'often associated with' in briefs and captions; offer several palettes per emotion; never promise sales/trust effects.
entries.limits: Cultural rules (mourning) must be respected regardless of experimental evidence.

entries.name: Thai colour of the day / birth-day colour
entries.label: HYPOTHESIS
entries.purpose: Each weekday has a colour (Sun red, Mon yellow, Tue pink, Wed green, Thu orange, Fri blue, Sat purple), linked to Hindu astrology and day Buddha images; one's birth-day colour is lucky.
entries.how: Optional day-themed posts; a light accent, not sales pressure; avoid royal birthday colours in commercial promos.
entries.limits: Source is tier E and details vary; confirm with Thai staff before use.

entries.name: Black and white = mourning
entries.label: EVIDENCE(news)+HYPOTHESIS
entries.purpose: Black/white are mourning colours in Thailand (nationwide during the 2016 royal mourning period); celebratory saturated palettes can offend in mourning contexts.
entries.how: During national mourning or condolence posts: monochrome or black/white with minimal accent; pause promo palettes.
entries.limits: Everyday black is fashion-neutral; context decides.

entries.name: Thai 'fa' (light blue) vs 'nam-ngoen' (dark blue)
entries.label: HYPOTHESIS
entries.purpose: Thai names light blue and dark blue separately; by analogy with Russian blue categories, Thai viewers may read a fa-to-nam-ngoen change as a different colour, not a shade.
entries.how: In Thai briefs say which one; keep a 'fa' background inside the light-blue category (high L) when the brief says fa.
entries.limits: Untested; Thai basic-term counts are disputed.

entries.name: Never code meaning by red vs green alone
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Several percent of men have red-green deficiency; observer metamerism means pairs that differ for you may match for them.
entries.how: Pair hue with a value difference, icon or label (sale tag shape + text); simulate with color_tools cvd.
entries.limits: Simulation approximates, not reproduces, individual experience.

entries.name: Text over photos: measure the worst local patch
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: WCAG counts insufficient contrast from background images as failure; photos vary under each glyph.
entries.how: Measure against the lightest (or darkest) area under the text; add a scrim/gradient band; aim above 4.5:1 for older eyewear customers.
entries.limits: Logotypes exempt; APCA only as a supplementary check.

entries.name: Blend and composite in linear light
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Averaging gamma-encoded sRGB values darkens and dulls midpoints; light adds linearly.
entries.how: Blurs, resizes, glows and light overlays on linearised values; CSS gradients in oklab interpolation.
entries.limits: Paint-like mixing needs a pigment model, not linear light.

entries.name: Pigment mixing vs light mixing
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Blue + yellow as light/RGB average gives grey; as paint gives green because pigments absorb and scatter repeatedly (Kubelka-Munk).
entries.how: Watercolour/gouache carousel styles: let the AI paint the overlaps or use a pigment mixer; do not fake paint overlaps with CSS blend modes.
entries.limits: Mixbox code licence reported as CC BY-NC (secondary); check before use.

entries.name: Auto white balance fails in one-colour scenes
entries.label: EVIDENCE+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Gray-world assumes the scene averages to grey; a frame dominated by sea, foliage or an orange wall drags the image toward the opposite cast.
entries.how: Shoot a grey card/white lens cloth in the same light, lock manual WB, or pick a known neutral in post before judging frame colour.
entries.limits: Learning-based camera AWB may do better than gray-world; still verify.

entries.name: Wide-gamut phone photos need gamut mapping to sRGB
entries.label: EVIDENCE+DERIVED
entries.purpose: iPhone images are often Display P3 (wider than sRGB); clipping on conversion flattens saturated greens/reds of acetate frames.
entries.how: Convert P3 to sRGB with a perceptual intent / gamut compression before compositing in HTML; compare saturated areas before/after.
entries.limits: Platform handling of embedded profiles varies; test on the target app.

entries.name: Rendering intent by content type
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Perceptual keeps gradations for photos; relative colorimetric keeps in-gamut colours exact for brand/proof; absolute for spot colours; saturation for charts.
entries.how: Shop flyers: photos perceptual, logo/brand colours relative colorimetric with a proof; never edit brand colour on an uncalibrated screen.
entries.limits: Perceptual and saturation intents are vendor-specific.

entries.name: Frame colour shifts between shop LEDs and daylight
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: Surfaces matching under one light can mismatch under another (metamer mismatching); low colour-rendition LEDs also distort hue/chroma.
entries.how: Show at least one daylight shot of each frame; when matching parts (front vs temples, frame vs case) check under both shop and window light; invite customers to check near the window.
entries.limits: Metamerism is uncommon in nature; frequency among acetate batches is a hypothesis.

entries.name: Product/try-on light: high fidelity, no red chroma loss
entries.label: EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: TM-30 research: perceived normalness and preference are driven by red chroma plus average fidelity; slight positive red chroma is preferred.
entries.how: Prefer lamps with high Rf (proposed: Rf>=80 and Rcs,h1 0..+8% for 'normal'; Rf>=74 with Rg>=100 for 'preferred'); do not mix lamp models/CCTs at one shooting table.
entries.limits: Criteria are one group's proposals summarised in DOE slides; datasheets often give only CRI Ra.

entries.name: Grade by moving one hue range, protect the rest
entries.label: EVIDENCE(case)+DERIVED
entries.purpose: A strong look can come from shifting one hue range across the whole film (O Brother: summer greens to dry browns/yellows) while touching little else.
entries.how: Hue-vs-hue/qualifier on the offending range (e.g. over-green AI foliage behind a product); protect skin and product hue; keep changes minimal to avoid artifacts.
entries.limits: Heavy secondaries on 8-bit AI images band quickly.

entries.name: Palette changes mark story turning points
entries.label: CRAFT
entries.purpose: A colour script keeps the palette stable within a beat and changes it at turning points so the audience feels the structure.
entries.how: One thumbnail per beat; note L/C/h and light relationship per beat; at most one big change per ~15 s in short clips.
entries.limits: No experimental evidence of audience effect; animation-studio craft.

entries.name: A motif colour tied to one meaning
entries.label: CRAFT+EVIDENCE
entries.purpose: A recurring colour linked to one character/object/idea (brand peach whenever the glasses help) builds meaning; meaning is inferred relative to the other colours used.
entries.how: Reserve the motif hue: do not use it on unrelated props; let it appear at each payoff beat.
entries.limits: Too many motifs cancel out.

entries.name: Value script for monochrome series
entries.label: CRAFT+DERIVED
entries.purpose: Charcoal/pencil stories have little hue, so the arc must live in value-key changes plus at most one accent.
entries.how: Problem slides mid-low key, resolution high key, accent only at the turning point; review the whole strip in greyscale.
entries.limits: Untested on our audience.
